Deadly Coal Run

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Carnage on the N2 near Pongola as coal merchants coin it, lives are being lost weekly

Unique Selling Point:
FOOTAGE OF ACCIDENTS, EMOTIONAL STORIES, POLITICIANS SHOWING UP AFTER MONTHS OF INACTION, COMMUNITY LEADERS UP AGAINST ALL ODDS

Summary:
On the 26th August, Jabu Hansen tweeted to transport minister Fikile Mbalula:
“Trucks are killing us on the Pongola N2, no traffic cops manning this route except local traffic cops when trucks get to town. We request your urgent intervention.

He never received a response.

Numerous accidents caused by reckless coal truck drivers have caused carnage along this stretch of highway. As the war in Ukraine pushed up export coal prices – there was money to be made on coal transport contracts and the mines and truckers are cashing in. Coal that used to go by rail down to Richards Bay has been transferred to roads because sabotage and looting has destroyed the Transnet rail system.

Adrian Channing Pierce has a farm that bisects the N2. He records truck violations and has counted the numbers of increased trucks on this road. In a 24 hour period he recorded 4300 trucks speeding down the highway. Adrian is a member of the local CPF and has been trying to turn the situation around. He says it is inconceivable that you add this many trucks and law enforcement is nowhere to be seen. At the same time there are only 12 traffic officers in Pongola and they are stretched to capacity. He says road worthy certificates and code 14 licenses are bought.



Further information:
In June this year Nico Van Vollenstee received a call from a man called Albert in Pongola. Albert is a car dealer and something of an unlikely angel who goes to accident scenes with his friend Jaco and they render assistance. Albert had found Nico’s business card in the wallet of his deceased son, one of four who had died instantly when a coal truck had overtaken on a blind corner, on a double white line. His son leaves behind two young children. Nico says the driver was released and never charged and he is probably back at work behind the wheel once more. He has no words for the ministers lack of action.

Craig Proctor Parker has spent over 30 years as a truck accident investigator. He also happens to collate data on trucks and accidents from everywhere he can. Now he has just been asked by a large insurer to put together that data for them, because insurers are coughing up masses in claims. He data shows increases in fatalities as an increasing number of trucks and inexperienced drivers under pressure to deliver – create horror scenes on our roads.



BLACK September
On Saturday 3rd of September there were 6 accidents on the N2 between Piet Retief and Richards Bay on the 3rd. But this was just the beginning. On the 16th September, even the politicians could no longer ignore the Pongola carnage. Adrian’s camera’s recorded the terrible scene. A fully laden coal truck overtaking another on a double white line smashed headlong into a white bakkie carrying school children. Twenty people died. Bodies lay strewn on the road and pinned under the truck as parents waited for hours for the forensic unit of SAPS to complete its work. One local mother lost three children, another two children. The driver ran away but later handed himself over to police and he is still in custody.

The N2 was closed because anger from the local community spilled onto the road. That evening Albert went to see if he could help his unarmed friend Jaco. He describes the rocks and broken glass on the road, the fear in the eyes of the motorists trapped on the road as the community threw rocks and began shooting. It was only the military presence he says that calmed the situation down. “It’s like a veld fire” he says, the community are angry about no services or delivery. The accident was the match that set it all alight. Then come the criminal elements hoping to loot or burn trucks on that stretch of highway”

So as the mothers mourned their dead, truckers moved onto a back road near Ulundi, hoping to save their trucks from being torched; the politicians took their blue lights and their million rand cars up the sand tracks to meet the mourning families, making promises they should have made many months before.

But where the trucks went the accidents followed. On a road near Ulundi, viral video of traffic officers directing traffic at the scene of another coal truck accident captures the moment when a second truck slams into a taxi and it explodes like a bomb. People are seen running for their lives and screams are heard from the scene. Miraculously – no one died in that accident. But still it was not over, says Albert. That evening at the same spot, another accident took place.

For now side tipper trucks are banned from the stretch of road between Pongola and Piet Retief until after the funerals. This weekend, the community will bury their children. No doubt the politicians will be there, but what happens after that when they climb back into their expensive cars? Carte Blanche tells this harrowing story, through the community leaders, the families and the ordinary people in Pongola screaming for help from a state that says it cares, but has yet to take any concrete action.

Script:


Deadly coal run FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX 09 October 2022

Voice Over 1
Pongola was once a quiet bushveld town.

Not anymore

Up sound coal truck

Coal trucks race right through it, to the port in Richards Bay- leaving death and destruction in their wake

Accidents

Locals tried to warn those in charge, but no- one was listening

FADE TO BLACK

Voice over 2
Jabulani Hansen is a community leader in Pongola.

Up sound Jabu talking to community

An industrial engineer with his own business making window frames, he cares about what happens in this northern KZN town

Up sound grinder

In 2019 he sent his first tweet to transport minister Fikile Mbalula. It was a warning and a cry for help.

Jabu 13th June 2019
we have no robots to control the traffic and it is only a matter of time before a huge accident that will take many lives happens.

Masa
And did you get a response?
Jabu
No I didn’t
Masa
But we have a minister of transport who is all over twitter?!
Jabu
That is what I thought! At least get a response, but nothing happened

Voice over 3
18 months later, Jabu’s worst fears were realized -and locals were unprepared for what was about to hit them on the N2


Bombs up sound

At the beginning of this year Russia invaded Ukraine, that left Europe with an energy crisis and coal in huge demand. Prices soared and miners in Mpumalanga cashed in.

Now towns along the N2 from Piet Retief to Richards Bay find themselves in a different battle.

Up sound coal truck

Coal trucks versus people.

Adrian Chaning -Pearce
When you drive down the road and these trucks are just driving at you, it almost feels like your life is not in your own hands anymore

Voice over 4
Adrian Chaning-Pearce’s farm is bisected by the N2. Like Jabu, this Pongola farmer is taking up the fight, against the deadly coal run.

Using technology, his cameras record truck transgressions.

Adrian
What we are seeing with a lot of these accidents is caused by slipstreaming or tailgating.
Obviously the drivers are paid bonuses or penalized on fuel consumption, so they all sit behind each other in a long train. If you are just a normal motorist and you want to overtake this train, sometimes you might have to overtake 8 or 9. In the event of someone at the front or in the middle of this train they hit their brakes, lose control and swerve into the oncoming traffic.

Voice over 5
For most of the year, an average of one coal truck every 30 seconds, would race past his farm

Up sound truck

But as the trucks increased, law enforcement says Adrian, virtually disappeared and like others in the town he suspects sinister interests may be at play

Adrian
What’s happening on the rail and the ports, it’s just too coincidental that all trucks arrive and law enforcement leave and it all happens overnight



Voice over 6
In June this year, just down the road from his farm, Adrian and local businessman Albert Brink arrived at this accident scene soon after it happened. Both men are still scarred by what they witnessed

Adrian
Like downtown Mogadishu with a bomb going off, there were literally bits of body and vehicles lying all over the road. It was horrendous

Voice over 7
A coal truck had swerved into the oncoming traffic and hit a group of friends and family travelling in two separate bakkies.

Albert up sound
The Ford ranger basically down the end there lying on its side. Two teenage male occupants survived, but the right side passengers were deceased, it literally looked like you had taken a grinder or a chainsaw and cut the vehicle open. It was horrendous

Albert
Now you can see how narrow this road is.
Masa
Ja it’s not safe actually
Albert
Its not safe at all I mean where you going to go
Masa
There is not even enough space for a car
Albert
That truck is going to hit you there is no other way

Voice over 8
Four people died here, one of them was Nico Von Vollenstee, and Albert had to tell his father, his son had died

Albert
I wouldn’t like that phone a stranger to say that my wife or family was in an accident and there is nothing left of them
Masa
What happened following that accident, did you see more law enforcement?
Albert
No unfortunately not. There was no improvement from local government side.

Voice over 9 Jabu Hansen
By August this year Jabu Hansen had not yet given up, and visited the KZN Dept of transport, but he was fobbed off.

Jabu
Unfortunately I was told that N2 is Sanral’s responsibility, and I was very disappointed.
Masa
So then you resorted to going back to Twitter?

Jabu
to minister Mbalula again, this was on the 26th August. Trucks are killing us on the Pongola N2, no traffic cops manning this route except local cops when trucks get to town, we request your urgent intervention.

Voice over 10
And he attached three videos to the tweet. This is one of them.

Up sound dashcam video- driver freaks out

Masa
And they still didn’t respond to the visuals you were posting, the tweets?
Jabu
No. They didn’t

Voice over 11
Exactly three weeks after Jabu sent his tweet to the minister, 18 children were coming back from school on a bakkie. It was hardly ideal, but their only means of transport

Dash cam of school accident

Voice over 12
All the children, and two adults were instantly killed.

Fade to black

Adrian took us through what happened

Adrian
The truck came all the way down that hill on the wrong side of the road/double barrier lines the whole way down, when he came around the corner first of all he narrowly missed a car,
Roughly where that chevron board is- that is where the collision occurred. It then pushed the bakkie straight through the taxi loading zone, it then with the bakkie underneath the truck pushed the bakkie all the way to our RHS here where the sand is in the culvert.
We had strewn bodies ...right to here where there were more bodies were trapped under the truck. It was a catastrophic collision there are no other words for it!

Voice over 13
These three little children were among the dead, lost in an instant to their mother, Nonhlanla and grandfather Enoch Ntshangase

Nonhlanhla
When I got there it was just sadness, the children were all over the ground, they were covered I was not able to see them immediately but I saw the shoes of my boy those were Thembelihle’s shoes, I thought maybe he would be going to hospital, he was one of the children on the ground. I was confused, and we were not allowed to see them until the people who took photographs arrived

Voice over 14
There are no forensic services in Pongola, so the family were forced to wait at the gruesome scene for hours

Nonhlanhla
Some of the other children were still under the truck, they were waiting for vehicles that were going to pick up the truck so that those kids can be taken from under the truck.

Enoch
I lost my mind, and I was confused as to whether they were dead or they would come back. I saw it, they had covered them on the road , those who saw them told me that these were people, this was a decapitated head, this is the brain lying over here, I was traumatised.

Voice over 15
Later, Enoch watched this video

Enoch
How did this happen? Even when I look at the video it’s as if I am dreaming. Was the driver a person or a ghost? Didn’t he see the van coming, because it’s as if he wasn’t seeing anything in front of him? He was driving at a high speed and bulldozing everything on the road

Voice over 16
The transport minister was finally paying attention, and flew rather than drove into KZN.

Masa
Now the politicians came but too late?
Jabu
It was too late, because a lot of us feel this could have been prevented

Voice over 17
Politicians fell over themselves to get to the crash site. Suddenly Pongola was swarming with police and traffic officers

Jabu Hansen
If we had that kind of police presence on the N2 on a daily basis to see them going all out for one man. That was a bitter pill to swallow for me

Adrian
Blue lights everywhere and then suddenly for two days we have a massive traffic police presence and suddenly its gone again

Fikile Mbalula 22nd September 2022
We are faced with serious challenges in terms of law enforcement
Voice over 18
Mbalula promised action. But why wait for a tragedy? Municipal manager Mtonjani Khali would have some answers

Masa
What is the plan of action?
Mr. Kali
Beef up my manpower, to get more traffic officers to be more visible every time on the road
Masa
As you planning as you are budgeting, people are dying on this road?
Mr. Kali
Ya, people are dying it’s not just a matter of planning and do it now, because there are costs involved, the only thing that gives you the go ahead, is the budget.

Voice over 19
He has also met with Pongola community and they want to see concrete action plans

Kali
We will not allow these coal trucks to move in for now, up until we have a plan

Voice over 20
As the families buried their loved ones, the coal trucks were banned from the N2 immediately following the accident. They were diverted from Piet Retief, onto the R34 and R66.

Link
But where the trucks went the accidents followed and horrific scenes of further carnage went viral on social media

Up sound driver
The truck was driving along R34....

Truck through first accident scene – fire ball

JEEZUS CHRIST! SHIT! BEEPTHIS

Voice over 21
Only three days after the horror school crash, this accident happened near Ulundi

Another accident again on the same place!

Rescuers were still busy cleaning up the first and second accidents, when incredibly a third accident happened

Up sound Afrikaans voice
There are five trucks again on the same place, so we are starting again. Here there is no time for rest.

Albert
Nine vehicles, nine trucks, one day, one single spot all in an accident!

Voice over 22
And that was just the beginning- Albert has been trying to keep track of the coal truck accidents on this diversion route

Diversion route crash montage

And he has counted 37 coal truck accidents in just 22 days on the R34 and R66, with no truck accidents on the N2 at Pongola since the coal trucks were diverted

Hymn up sound

As the families still mourn the departed, the driver that killed the children, remains in custody. The coal truckers are impatient to drive the N2 once more, but Pongola residents insist on visible and meaningful change first.

The transport minister has made promises to improve the rail network just as Transnet goes on strike. So the battle between trucks and people is far from over.

THE END 13 10

PROMO ONE 11 seconds
Local residents of Pongola tried to warn authorities that coal trucks on the N2 were endangering their lives, but no one listened until tragedy struck

PROMO TWO
A war in Ukraine sent the export coal prices soaring, but the residents of Pongola are paying the price with their lives as coal trucks dash down the N2 to the port of Richards Bay

Adrian
When you drive down the road and these trucks are just driving at you, it almost feels like your life is not in your own hands anymore

It took a horror smash to get authorities attention

PROMO THREE
A spike in the export coal price, a broken rail system, an absence of law enforcement and reckless truck drivers wanting to cash in, has caused havoc on the N2 since February
Jabu
Masa
Now the politicians came but too late?
Jabu
It was too late, because a lot of us feel this could have been prevented

Prices soared and miners in Mpumalanga cashed in. Now towns along the N2 from Piet Retief to Richards Bay find themselves in a different battle. Up sound coal truck Coal trucks versus people. Adrian Chaning -Pearce When you drive down the road and these trucks are just driving at you, it almost feels like your life is not in your own hands anymore Voice over 4 Adrian Chaning-Pearce’s farm is bisected by the N2. Like Jabu, this Pongola farmer is taking up the fight, against the deadly coal run. Using technology, his cameras record truck transgressions. Adrian What we are seeing with a lot of these accidents is caused by slipstreaming or tailgating. Obviously the drivers are paid bonuses or penalized on fuel consumption, so they all sit behind each other in a long train. If you are just a normal motorist and you want to overtake this train, sometimes you might have to overtake 8 or 9. In the event of someone at the front or in the middle of this train they hit their brakes, lose control and swerve into the oncoming traffic. Voice over 5 For most of the year, an average of one coal truck every 30 seconds, would race past his farm Up sound truck But as the trucks increased, law enforcement says Adrian, virtually disappeared and like others in the town he suspects sinister interests may be at play Adrian What’s happening on the rail and the ports, it’s just too coincidental that all trucks arrive and law enforcement leave and it all happens overnight Voice over 6 In June this year, just down the road from his farm, Adrian and local businessman Albert Brink arrived at this accident scene soon after it happened. Both men are still scarred by what they witnessed Adrian Like downtown Mogadishu with a bomb going off, there were literally bits of body and vehicles lying all over the road. It was horrendous Voice over 7 A coal truck had swerved into the oncoming traffic and hit a group of friends and family travelling in two separate bakkies. Albert up sound The Ford ranger basically down the end there lying on its side. Two teenage male occupants survived, but the right side passengers were deceased, it literally looked like you had taken a grinder or a chainsaw and cut the vehicle open. It was horrendous Albert Now you can see how narrow this road is. Masa Ja it’s not safe actually Albert Its not safe at all I mean where you going to go Masa There is not even enough space for a car Albert That truck is going to hit you there is no other way Voice over 8 Four people died here, one of them was Nico Von Vollenstee, and Albert had to tell his father, his son had died Albert I wouldn’t like that phone a stranger to say that my wife or family was in an accident and there is nothing left of them Masa What happened following that accident, did you see more law enforcement? Albert No unfortunately not. There was no improvement from local government side. Voice over 9 Jabu Hansen By August this year Jabu Hansen had not yet given up, and visited the KZN Dept of transport, but he was fobbed off. Jabu Unfortunately I was told that N2 is Sanral’s responsibility, and I was very disappointed. Masa So then you resorted to going back to Twitter? Jabu to minister Mbalula again, this was on the 26th August. Trucks are killing us on the Pongola N2, no traffic cops manning this route except local cops when trucks get to town, we request your urgent intervention. Voice over 10 And he attached three videos to the tweet. This is one of them. Up sound dashcam video- driver freaks out Masa And they still didn’t respond to the visuals you were posting, the tweets? Jabu No. They didn’t Voice over 11 Exactly three weeks after Jabu sent his tweet to the minister, 18 children were coming back from school on a bakkie. It was hardly ideal, but their only means of transport Dash cam of school accident Voice over 12 All the children, and two adults were instantly killed. Fade to black Adrian took us through what happened Adrian The truck came all the way down that hill on the wrong side of the road/double barrier lines the whole way down, when he came around the corner first of all he narrowly missed a car, Roughly where that chevron board is- that is where the collision occurred. It then pushed the bakkie straight through the taxi loading zone, it then with the bakkie underneath the truck pushed the bakkie all the way to our RHS here where the sand is in the culvert. We had strewn bodies ...right to here where there were more bodies were trapped under the truck. It was a catastrophic collision there are no other words for it! Voice over 13 These three little children were among the dead, lost in an instant to their mother, Nonhlanla and grandfather Enoch Ntshangase Nonhlanhla When I got there it was just sadness, the children were all over the ground, they were covered I was not able to see them immediately but I saw the shoes of my boy those were Thembelihle’s shoes, I thought maybe he would be going to hospital, he was one of the children on the ground. I was confused, and we were not allowed to see them until the people who took photographs arrived Voice over 14 There are no forensic services in Pongola, so the family were forced to wait at the gruesome scene for hours Nonhlanhla Some of the other children were still under the truck, they were waiting for vehicles that were going to pick up the truck so that those kids can be taken from under the truck. Enoch I lost my mind, and I was confused as to whether they were dead or they would come back. I saw it, they had covered them on the road , those who saw them told me that these were people, this was a decapitated head, this is the brain lying over here, I was traumatised. Voice over 15 Later, Enoch watched this video Enoch How did this happen? Even when I look at the video it’s as if I am dreaming. Was the driver a person or a ghost? Didn’t he see the van coming, because it’s as if he wasn’t seeing anything in front of him? He was driving at a high speed and bulldozing everything on the road Voice over 16 The transport minister was finally paying attention, and flew rather than drove into KZN. Masa Now the politicians came but too late? Jabu It was too late, because a lot of us feel this could have been prevented Voice over 17 Politicians fell over themselves to get to the crash site. Suddenly Pongola was swarming with police and traffic officers Jabu Hansen If we had that kind of police presence on the N2 on a daily basis to see them going all out for one man. That was a bitter pill to swallow for me Adrian Blue lights everywhere and then suddenly for two days we have a massive traffic police presence and suddenly its gone again Fikile Mbalula 22nd September 2022 We are faced with serious challenges in terms of law enforcement Voice over 18 Mbalula promised action. But why wait for a tragedy? Municipal manager Mtonjani Khali would have some answers Masa What is the plan of action? Mr. Kali Beef up my manpower, to get more traffic officers to be more visible every time on the road Masa As you planning as you are budgeting, people are dying on this road? Mr. Kali Ya, people are dying it’s not just a matter of planning and do it now, because there are costs involved, the only thing that gives you the go ahead, is the budget. Voice over 19 He has also met with Pongola community and they want to see concrete action plans Kali We will not allow these coal trucks to move in for now, up until we have a plan Voice over 20 As the families buried their loved ones, the coal trucks were banned from the N2 immediately following the accident. They were diverted from Piet Retief, onto the R34 and R66. Link But where the trucks went the accidents followed and horrific scenes of further carnage went viral on social media Up sound driver The truck was driving along R34.... Truck through first accident scene – fire ball JEEZUS CHRIST! SHIT! BEEPTHIS Voice over 21 Only three days after the horror school crash, this accident happened near Ulundi Another accident again on the same place! Rescuers were still busy cleaning up the first and second accidents, when incredibly a third accident happened Up sound Afrikaans voice There are five trucks again on the same place, so we are starting again. Here there is no time for rest. Albert Nine vehicles, nine trucks, one day, one single spot all in an accident! Voice over 22 And that was just the beginning- Albert has been trying to keep track of the coal truck accidents on this diversion route Diversion route crash montage And he has counted 37 coal truck accidents in just 22 days on the R34 and R66, with no truck accidents on the N2 at Pongola since the coal trucks were diverted Hymn up sound As the families still mourn the departed, the driver that killed the children, remains in custody. The coal truckers are impatient to drive the N2 once more, but Pongola residents insist on visible and meaningful change first. The transport minister has made promises to improve the rail network just as Transnet goes on strike. So the battle between trucks and people is far from over. THE END 13 10 PROMO ONE 11 seconds Local residents of Pongola tried to warn authorities that coal trucks on the N2 were endangering their lives, but no one listened until tragedy struck PROMO TWO A war in Ukraine sent the export coal prices soaring, but the residents of Pongola are paying the price with their lives as coal trucks dash down the N2 to the port of Richards Bay Adrian When you drive down the road and these trucks are just driving at you, it almost feels like your life is not in your own hands anymore It took a horror smash to get authorities attention PROMO THREE A spike in the export coal price, a broken rail system, an absence of law enforcement and reckless truck drivers wanting to cash in, has caused havoc on the N2 since February Jabu Masa Now the politicians came but too late? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Carnage on the N2 near Pongola as coal merchants coin it, lives are being lost weekly
metadata.Unique Selling Point: FOOTAGE OF ACCIDENTS, EMOTIONAL STORIES, POLITICIANS SHOWING UP AFTER MONTHS OF INACTION, COMMUNITY LEADERS UP AGAINST ALL ODDS
metadata.Summary: On the 26th August, Jabu Hansen tweeted to transport minister Fikile Mbalula: “Trucks are killing us on the Pongola N2, no traffic cops manning this route except local traffic cops when trucks get to town. We request your urgent intervention. He never received a response. Numerous accidents caused by reckless coal truck drivers have caused carnage along this stretch of highway. As the war in Ukraine pushed up export coal prices – there was money to be made on coal transport contracts and the mines and truckers are cashing in. Coal that used to go by rail down to Richards Bay has been transferred to roads because sabotage and looting has destroyed the Transnet rail system. Adrian Channing Pierce has a farm that bisects the N2. He records truck violations and has counted the numbers of increased trucks on this road. In a 24 hour period he recorded 4300 trucks speeding down the highway. Adrian is a member of the local CPF and has been trying to turn the situation around. He says it is inconceivable that you add this many trucks and law enforcement is nowhere to be seen. At the same time there are only 12 traffic officers in Pongola and they are stretched to capacity. He says road worthy certificates and code 14 licenses are bought.
metadata.Further information: In June this year Nico Van Vollenstee received a call from a man called Albert in Pongola. Albert is a car dealer and something of an unlikely angel who goes to accident scenes with his friend Jaco and they render assistance. Albert had found Nico’s business card in the wallet of his deceased son, one of four who had died instantly when a coal truck had overtaken on a blind corner, on a double white line. His son leaves behind two young children. Nico says the driver was released and never charged and he is probably back at work behind the wheel once more. He has no words for the ministers lack of action. Craig Proctor Parker has spent over 30 years as a truck accident investigator. He also happens to collate data on trucks and accidents from everywhere he can. Now he has just been asked by a large insurer to put together that data for them, because insurers are coughing up masses in claims. He data shows increases in fatalities as an increasing number of trucks and inexperienced drivers under pressure to deliver – create horror scenes on our roads. BLACK September On Saturday 3rd of September there were 6 accidents on the N2 between Piet Retief and Richards Bay on the 3rd. But this was just the beginning. On the 16th September, even the politicians could no longer ignore the Pongola carnage. Adrian’s camera’s recorded the terrible scene. A fully laden coal truck overtaking another on a double white line smashed headlong into a white bakkie carrying school children. Twenty people died. Bodies lay strewn on the road and pinned under the truck as parents waited for hours for the forensic unit of SAPS to complete its work. One local mother lost three children, another two children. The driver ran away but later handed himself over to police and he is still in custody. The N2 was closed because anger from the local community spilled onto the road. That evening Albert went to see if he could help his unarmed friend Jaco. He describes the rocks and broken glass on the road, the fear in the eyes of the motorists trapped on the road as the community threw rocks and began shooting. It was only the military presence he says that calmed the situation down. “It’s like a veld fire” he says, the community are angry about no services or delivery. The accident was the match that set it all alight. Then come the criminal elements hoping to loot or burn trucks on that stretch of highway” So as the mothers mourned their dead, truckers moved onto a back road near Ulundi, hoping to save their trucks from being torched; the politicians took their blue lights and their million rand cars up the sand tracks to meet the mourning families, making promises they should have made many months before. But where the trucks went the accidents followed. On a road near Ulundi, viral video of traffic officers directing traffic at the scene of another coal truck accident captures the moment when a second truck slams into a taxi and it explodes like a bomb. People are seen running for their lives and screams are heard from the scene. Miraculously – no one died in that accident. But still it was not over, says Albert. That evening at the same spot, another accident took place. For now side tipper trucks are banned from the stretch of road between Pongola and Piet Retief until after the funerals. This weekend, the community will bury their children. No doubt the politicians will be there, but what happens after that when they climb back into their expensive cars? Carte Blanche tells this harrowing story, through the community leaders, the families and the ordinary people in Pongola screaming for help from a state that says it cares, but has yet to take any concrete action.
